verdict.rationale: The Trusted Agent Protocol gives merchants the identification layer for allow/deny decisions. Agents present RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures that merchants verify against Visa's public keys, so they can tell credentialed agents from anonymous bots. Merchants can also reject replayed or expired signatures, and the reference implementation ships an agent-registry and a cdn-proxy verifier. However, the evidence shows verification primitives the merchant must build policy on top of, not a merchant-facing control surface. Missing for 10: documented rate-limiting of agents, explicit per-agent or per-platform allowlist/denylist configuration, a merchant policy dashboard or API, and independent hands-on corroboration.
